_comment: USG RADIUS - EAP-TLS and RadSec with certificate revocation checking (CRL/OCSP)
_description: Supplicant certificates (EAP-TLS) and NAS certificates (RadSec) are checked against a CRL and/or OCSP at TLS handshake time, after chain validation against the CA bundle. Needs a binary built with the `revocation` cargo feature (the container image and release binary are).
_revocation_notes: on_error: fail_closed (default) rejects the client when the status cannot be determined (CRL/OCSP unreachable, stale, unparseable, or nothing covers the certificate's issuer); fail_open accepts and logs a warning. A positive 'revoked' answer always rejects.

crl.static_files: CRL files (PEM or DER) loaded at startup and matched to certificates by issuer; refresh them and restart before nextUpdate, or the check fails per on_error. Recommended for air-gapped sites.

crl.fetch: follow the certificate's CRL Distribution Points over HTTP(S) when no current static CRL covers its issuer. The fetch blocks that handshake for up to crl.fetch_timeout_secs, so keep it short relative to the NAS's RADIUS timeout. Fetched CRLs are cached for crl.cache_ttl_secs (and never past their nextUpdate).

ocsp.*: responder URL comes from the certificate's Authority Information Access extension; the issuer certificate is taken from the CA bundle. A nonce (RFC 8954) is sent and must be echoed when ocsp.nonce is true. OCSP response signatures are not verified in this release, so prefer crl_only unless the responder path is trusted.
eap.tls.revocation requires eap.tls.require_client_cert = true and eap.tls.ca_path; radsec.revocation applies to the NAS client certificates RadSec always verifies.
Every field under crl and ocsp is optional; the values below are the defaults except where noted.
